summary: Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London (~1871–1875) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1875–1879). He taught Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and held posts at the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926) and the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901).

Alfred Edward Housman worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Bromsgrove School, King Edward's School, and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881). He held a post at University College London (~1892–1911) and taught Mortimer Wheeler.

Alfred Ernout was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1944), the University of Paris (~1927–1946), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

Alfred Espinas worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1860–1864) and the École Normale Supérieure (~1864–1867). He held a post at the University of Paris (~1894–1912) and taught Marcel Mauss.

Alfred Forke worked in sinology and philosophy after studying at the University of Geneva (~1886–1887) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1889). He held posts at Humboldt University, the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), and the University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE, and the University of Paris, and founded DAFA in 1922.

Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Ronald Leach and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics. He held posts at the University of Sussex, Australian National University, and the London School of Economics.

Alfred Hillebrandt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Munich under Martin Haug, later holding associate and full professorships at the University of Breslau from 1883 onward.

Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890). He held posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig, and taught Albert Debrunner.

Alfred Ludwig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Bonitz, Boller, Boeckh, Haupt, and Weber. He held posts at the University of Vienna and Charles University.

Alfred Métraux studied at the École des chartes, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he studied under Marcel Mauss. He later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1959–1963).

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney, University of Chicago, University of Oxford, and FESP in São Paulo, and taught Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas.
Ali S. Asani works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard College (~1973–1977) and Harvard University (~1977–1984), where he became a professor around 1983.
Alice Y. Tseng works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang (attested 2005) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2013).

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago (attested 2009), supervised by Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and also studied under Saw Tun, Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She was supervised for her doctorate by Martin King Whyte and also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Alka Patel works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned a bachelor's degree from Mount Holyoke College and a PhD from Harvard University, later becoming an associate professor at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Allan G. Grapard was a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a Ph.D. at INALCO. He held posts at the University of California and UC Santa Barbara from 1985 to 2011.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (B.A.) and Harvard University (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), the University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016), and taught Charles Goodman.

Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford in 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001) and taught Alison Denton Jones.
